speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long you have been experiencing this chronic cough, and have you noticed any blood in your sputum? Also, could you quantify how much weight you have lost over the past few months?

text: 68-year-old male. The patient reports having a fever, cough, weakness, night sweats, and poor appetite persisting for 6 months. He has lost 7.5 kg (16.5 lb) over this period. No history of breathlessness, nasal discharge, nasal obstruction, palpitations, chest pain, or digestive symptoms. Released from prison 9 months ago after a 2-year sentence.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent release from prison, I need to ask if you were exposed to anyone with tuberculosis or if you were screened for it during your incarceration. I will also need to check your vital signs and listen to your lungs for any abnormal sounds.

text: With normal CBC and CT but persistent symptoms and a history of incarceration, I suspect drug-resistant TB or a missed diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Sputum_Nucleic_Acid_Amplification_Test

speaker: Doctor
text: Since all standard tests for tuberculosis are negative and the CT scan is normal, I must consider non-infectious causes such as lymphoma or sarcoidosis. Do you have any history of skin rashes, joint pain, or eye inflammation? REQUEST TEST: Bronchoscopy_with_Biopsy

speaker: Doctor
text: With all infectious and neoplastic workups returning normal, I must consider a functional or psychosomatic etiology given the lack of objective findings.
